title: Maha Shivaratri: the great night of Shiva
hookLine: a night kept awake, water poured over the lingam, Om Namah Shivaya until dawn
carry: bholenath: shiva is pleased by the smallest offering
tomorrow: Raksha Bandhan: the thread of protection
last: THE NAME OF GOD OUTLASTS THE FIRE.

cards: This festival happens in the dark. Once a year, on the fourteenth night of the waning moon, just before the new moon, in late winter, Shiva temples stay open all night. The lines go around the block.
People carry small brass pots of water and milk. They've been fasting since morning, and they're not going to bed.
Inside, the sound doesn't stop: a bell, a chant, Om Namah Shivaya, again and again, until the sky starts to go gray. It's called Maha Shivaratri, the great night of Shiva.
And one story people tell about it is about a man who stayed awake by accident.

teach.b: The story comes from the Shiva Purana. A hunter goes into the forest, catches nothing all day, and night falls. Afraid of wild animals, he climbs a tree to wait for morning.
It happens to be a bilva tree, whose three-part leaves are sacred to Shiva.

teach.h: LEAVES FALL ON A HIDDEN STONE.
teach.b: And at its foot, hidden in the dark, is a Shiva lingam, the smooth rounded stone that stands for Shiva in temples. The hunter has no idea.
All night, to stay awake and keep watch, he fidgets, and leaves drop from the branches onto the stone below. Water spills from his flask onto it. He hasn't eaten.
He doesn't sleep. By dawn, without meaning to, he has done everything this night asks: fasted, kept awake, offered water and bilva leaves to Shiva.
In the tellings, when deer come by he lets them go, and his heart changes. And Shiva frees him. His intention wasn't holy.
He was just scared and stuck in a tree.
That's why Shiva is called Bholenath, the simple-hearted lord, and Ashutosh, the one quickly pleased. He doesn't ask for gold. A pot of water, a leaf, a night awake.
So that's what people do on Shivaratri; ratri means night.
They fast, keep a vigil through the night's four watches, and pour water, milk or honey over the lingam, an offering called abhisheka, then lay bilva leaves on top.

teach.h: SHIVA IS PLEASED BY THE SMALLEST OFFERING.
teach.b: Different families remember different reasons for the night. Some say it's Shiva's wedding to Parvati, some say his dance; i'll come back to those.

how: On Maha Shivaratri many Hindus fast, visit Shiva temples, pour water, milk or honey over the Shiva lingam with bilva leaves, and keep a vigil through the night chanting Om Namah Shivaya until dawn.

o: a midday feast for Shiva's devotees
the night of Shiva, kept awake

games.q: what's inside the night — tap the pairs.
p: the three-part leaf sacred to Shiva
pouring water or milk over the lingam

s: Shivaratri is kept during the day
it's a night festival: people keep a vigil until dawn.
in the story, Shiva ignored the hunter because he didn't mean to worship
Shiva freed him anyway. that's why he's called Bholenath: pleased by the smallest offering.
people remember different reasons for the night
some say Shiva's wedding to Parvati, some say his dance; the vigil is kept for all of them.

games.q: you're the hunter. it's dark, the forest is full of animals, and you've caught nothing. what do you do?
o: climb a tree and wait for morning.
light a fire on the ground and sleep.
games.why: he climbs a bilva tree and stays awake all night. leaves and water fall onto a hidden lingam, and he keeps Shivaratri without knowing it.

practice: Sit, and lower your eyes. If you pray, say Om Namah Shivaya, slowly, once with each breath out. If you have a little water nearby, pour a few drops onto a plant or the earth, the simplest offering there is.
If you don't pray, just watch your breath. When something in you says that's enough, take three more. Like the hunter on his branch: not holy, just staying.

wordCard.voice: Shivaratri. The night of Shiva. Once a year, the great one, kept awake until dawn.

orig.note: Sanskrit: shiva, the kind or auspicious one, and ratri, night.

carryVoice: Your line: bholenath, shiva is pleased by the smallest offering. A leaf, some water, a night. Eighty-three days in.
